title: Intention different from discernment to kill
keywords: children in conflict with the law
primary_topics: Tacloban shooting by two young boys -- grief, anger, and confusion between the legal concepts of discernment and criminal intent: can a child intend to shoot yet lack discernment to be criminally liable?

Section 6 of RA 9344 (Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act), as amended by RA 10630 -- children 15 or under exempt; above 15 and below 18 exempt unless they acted with discernment; age computed at midnight of the birth date

Definitions -- discernment (CICL XXX v. People, 2023) is the capacity to understand right and wrong and the consequences; intent is the desire of the act, discernment the moral significance ascribed to it (Guevarra v. Almodovar, 1989)

Application -- 14-year-old 'Nash' exempt and subject to an intervention program regardless of intent; 15-year-old 'Rod' found by DSWD to have acted with discernment, no diversion because the penalty exceeds six years, now under preliminary investigation for three counts of murder
Lowering the age of criminal liability -- first address technology and social media, incl. nihilistic and violent extremist groups like '764', which distort children's capacity to discern
Closing -- institutions bear the paramount responsibility to guide youth; children are often victims of a society that failed to protect them; nurture them to hold pens, books and devices, not guns

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban contrasts the grief over two young athletes lost to the waves of Dipaculao, Aurora with the darker grief over the Tacloban shooting, in which two young boys killed many. He notes how discernment and criminal intent are easily confused and asks whether a child can intend to shoot yet lack the discernment to be criminally liable. Section 6 of RA 9344, as amended by RA 10630, exempts children 15 or under; those above 15 and below 18 are also exempt and placed in intervention unless they acted with discernment. A child is 15 at midnight of the birth date and crosses into the next bracket after the following midnight. CICL XXX v. People (2023) defines discernment as the child's capacity to understand right and wrong and the consequences of the wrongful act; Guevarra v. Almodovar (1989) explains that intent is the desire of one's act while discernment is the moral significance ascribed to it, and that intelligence, including discernment, is needed for a crime to exist. So a child may intend to pull a trigger yet lack discernment, and the law's rationale rests on discernment, not intent. Applying this, 14-year-old 'Nash' is exempt and subject to an intervention program, however deliberate his intent; 15-year-old 'Rod,' whom DSWD found to have acted with discernment, cannot undergo diversion because the penalty exceeds six years and is under preliminary investigation for three counts of murder. On proposals to lower the age of criminal liability to 10 or 12, CJP urges first addressing what RA 9344's framers could not anticipate: technology, social media and extremist groups like '764' that distort children's capacity to discern. Institutions bear the paramount responsibility to guide youth; true justice means nurturing children to hold pens, books and digital devices, not guns.
